projects.summary: Zyrite 是 ZYAILLC 团队做的开源 Markdown 桌面编辑器。原文、实时预览和所见即所得放在同一个窗口里，打开一个文件夹就是一个笔记库。文件始终是你磁盘上的普通 .md，不用注册账号，也不经过我们的服务器。 完整的 Markdown 写作 三种写法：原文和预览两栏同步滚动、实时预览、所见即所得。所见即所得保存时只重写你改过的块，改一个词，git diff 里就只有一行。 CommonMark + GFM（表格、任务列表、脚注）、YAML frontmatter、KaTeX 公式和化学式。 Mermaid、Graphviz、Markmap 图表，100 多种语言的代码高亮，全部本地渲染，不联网。 Obsidian 语法：[[双链]]、图片和章节嵌入、#标签、callout、==高亮==，从 Obsidian 搬过来的笔记不用改。 正则查找替换、多光标、专注模式、打字机模式。 多文件编辑 打开任意文件夹就有文件树和大纲，外部增删改文件即时同步。 双链补全；重命名或移动笔记时，可以一并更新指向它的链接。 命令面板、快速打开、全文搜索，中文不用分词也能搜到。 也能打开 YAML、JSON、TOML、配置文件、CSV、代码和日志，带语法高亮；JSON / YAML / TOML 边写边校验。GBK、Big5 等旧编码自动识别，按原编码写回。 其他 审阅 AI Agent 的改动：Claude Code、Cursor、Codex 改了文件，Zyrite 按块标出改动，逐处接受或拒绝；内置 MCP 服务，支持页边批注。 导出 PDF、HTML、Word（不需要装 pandoc），PDF 的公式、图表和中文排版与预览一致。 选中文字可以用 AI 润色、续写、翻译。内置 DeepSeek、通义千问、智谱、Kimi、豆包、腾讯混元、文心、Claude、Gemini、Grok 等 26 个模型服务，也能用 ChatGPT 套餐登录，或者接 Ollama 等本地模型。密钥存在系统钥匙串里。 基于 Tauri + Rust + React，支持 macOS、Windows、Linux，Apache-2.0 许可。macOS 和 Windows 安装包都不到 9 MB。界面默认英文，可以在设置里切换为简体中文。

projects.title: 【开源自荐】phonedriver：让 Claude Code、Codex 等 AI 智能体操作 Android 手机和 iPhone 的开源工具
projects.author: hridaya423

github.name: hridaya423/phonedriver
github.description: Open-source MCP server and CLI that lets AI agents like Claude Code see and control Android and iOS phones.

projects.summary: 自荐：我是 phonedriver 的作者。我不会中文，这段介绍是机器翻译的，有不通顺的地方请见谅。 phonedriver 是一个免费、开源（AGPL-3.0）的 MCP 服务器和命令行工具，用 Rust 编写。它让 Claude Code、Codex、Cursor 等 AI 智能体直接使用 Android 手机或 iPhone：读取屏幕、点击、输入、滑动，任何 App 都可以，不需要 App 提供 API。 智能体看到的不是截图，而是一份带编号的文本列表，按编号点击；每次操作后只返回发生变化的那几行。 Android 上不需要安装 App。phonedriver 通过 adb 用 appprocess 启动一个常驻的小进程（和 scrcpy 的做法相同），让无障碍连接一直保持着。 速度：在一台 Android 17 模拟器上读取 1000 行的列表，p50 为 12.7 ms，adb shell uiautomator dump 为 2163.7 ms。在 HONOR X8 真机上是 78.5 ms 对 2506.6 ms。 点到 Pay、Place order、Delete account 这类按钮时，工具会拦住这次点击，先在客户端里询问用户。 也可以用来测试自己的 App：我在一个注册表单里埋了两个 bug，Claude 用 49 秒把两个都找了出来，并写出了复现步骤。 局限：速度数据主要来自模拟器，真机只测过一台 HONOR X8；iOS 需要一台装有 Xcode 的 Mac。基准测试的方法和原始数据都是公开的： 安装：claude mcp add phonedriver -- npx -y phonedriver mcp 仓库里有中文 README。欢迎反馈。

projects.title: [分享创造] 一个带来源分级与保鲜机制的海外项目数据集（41 项目 / 136 来源，开源 + 双语站）
projects.summary: 做这个小东西的起因很具体：在给自己查 2027 年 J-1 的资格，发现中文世界关于「打工度假 / 海外实习签证」的信息有一个系统性问题—— 把只对中国台湾、中国香港护照开放的项目，写成「中国公民可申请」。加拿大 IEC 、英国 YMS 、爱尔兰 WHA 、日本 WH 、韩国 H-1 都属于双边互惠协议，中国大陆护照不在名单内。这类错误在攻略、中介软文、AI 生成内容里反复出现。 于是我把它当成一个数据工程问题来做，而不是又一个攻略站。 是什么 开源数据集 + 一个双语静态站。41 个项目、21 个国家和地区、136 条来源，其中中国大陆护照可申 34 个、不可申 7 个（不可申的也明确收录，作为排除记录）。 站： https://eddieye1004.github.io/overseas-program-dataset/ 库： https://github.com/eddieye1004/overseas-program-dataset 怎么做的 1) schema 先行。每个项目一个 JSON ，字段定义在 data/schema.json ，护照资格是第一等公民（ passport_types 决定 90% 的结论）。 2) 来源分级 + CI 强制。每条来源标 primary/secondary ，并按域名分 A/B/C/D 四级：A 是移民局/使领馆/官方法规库，D 是百科、自媒体、商业博客。D 级出现即 CI 失败，全部来源都不到 A/B 级也失败。二手来源不能单独支撑硬性资格判定。 3) 保鲜靠台账而不是靠人记。每条记录带 last_verified 。scripts/track.py 按项目性质分档：窗口写死到具体日期的 90 天复核、其余 180 天，剩余不足 25% 提前标「即将到期」。 产物两份：tracking.json 给程序读，FRESHNESS.md 给人读。CI 每周一跑 --check ，超期即退出码 1 把构建打红；另有一个脚本把同一份台账同步成一张 issue （固定标题 + 固定标签，先搜后改，不刷屏），让「红了」这件事真的有人看到。 4) 配额四态化（刚做完的一轮）。原来是「整数或 null 」，而 null 同时兼指「无名额上限 / 官方设限额但未公布 / 还没查」三种，读的人分不出来——他根本不知道自己看到的那一格是「没有上限」还是「没查」。 现在改成一个必填的状态字段，四态：有具体配额 / 无配额 / 官方未公布数字 / 待核实。凡断言前三态都必须指向本项目已有的一条 primary 来源，指不出来就只能写「待核实」。当前分布 4 / 34 / 1 / 2 。 两条「待核实」我没有硬凑数字——一个是奥地利红白红卡高资质档，NAG 有联邦最高限额制度，但这一档是否在限额之内、当年数字多少，官网几个页面都查不到；一个是德国机会卡，法条只授权联邦政府可限量、本身不设数字，配套条例经查不存在。这两条就挂在待办清单里，不写成「无配额」。 现在的状态 validate 严格模式 0 错 0 警； 135 个 Python 测试； e2e 212 条断言；前端 tsc/smoke/build 全绿。 窗口日历也做成了硬分区：41 个项目里 3 个能给出官方已公布的日期、2 个只敢按往年规律推断、36 个无从判断——这 36 个里有 32 个本身就是滚动受理、没有固定窗口，其余可查的已逐个核查并在条目里写明卡点。推断与「无从判断」两块在页面上永不出现具体日期。 没有 star 数可以报，也没有用户量可以报——就是我自己在用的一个库。 想求什么反馈 1) 数据纠错入口刚上线（结构化 issue 表单，必填官方来源），最想要的是**挑错**：哪条资格写错了、哪条链接死了、哪个数字过期了。附上官方页面链接就行。 表单： https://github.com/eddieye1004/overseas-program-dataset/issues/new?template=data-correction.yml 2) 来源分级的标准是否合理——特别是「高校官方部门算 C 级、只能作旁证」这条，我拿不准是不是过于严格。 3) 如果你在做同类项目，想听你怎么解决「保鲜」这件事。 不做的事也写清楚：不代办、不做中介导流、不提供「你该申哪个」的建议。这是信息汇编，判断留给你自己。

projects.title: 【开源自荐】Lean Init IDE：在浏览器里跑真正的 Lean 4 语言服务器
projects.author: 3y3y3y-huaiji

github.name: 3y3y3y-huaiji/lean-init-ide
github.description: Browser-native Lean 4 Init IDE: a real LSP in a Web Worker, 22 interactive lessons, zero install.

projects.summary: 学 Lean 4 之前通常要先在本地装工具链、配编辑器插件，不少人卡在这一步就没往下学。我做了一个运行在浏览器里的 Lean 4 练习环境，不用装任何本地软件，打开网页就能写证明、看报错和实时 Goal。 编译器和语言服务器（Lean 4.34.1）以 WebAssembly 跑在浏览器 Web Worker 里，所有检查和求值都在本地完成，代码不会上传。 首次点击「启动 Lean」会下载约 102MB 的运行时（用 zstd 压缩并做了分片校验，国内会优先走镜像），之后走浏览器缓存。 编辑器基于 Monaco，接了真实的语义补全、悬停提示和报错跳转，输入 \to、\forall 这类缩写会自动转成对应的 Unicode 符号。 配套写了 22 节中英双语入门课，从基础逻辑一直讲到归纳、素数和插入排序验证。页内代码块点一下就能直接运行（复用进程，一般不到半秒出结果），练习会带到编辑器并自动保存草稿。

projects.summary: 自荐：我是 o8 的作者。 o8 是一个免费、开源（MIT）的桌面应用，专门负责审查和合并 AI 编程代理写出来的代码。代码可以在任何地方写：Claude Code、Codex、Cursor 或你自己的编辑器。写完交给 o8，由另一个独立的代理（最好是不同的模型）审查真实的 diff，把问题退回给作者修改，修完再审，通过后合并。 写代码的代理不能给自己的代码放行。审查由另一个代理完成，批准结果绑定到它审查的那个 commit，代码再改动，批准就失效。 审查不通过时，问题清单会退回给原作者代理修改，最多两轮，每一步都留有记录。 不绑定模型和工具。o8 调用你机器上已经装好的代理 CLI（Claude Code、Codex、OpenCode、Gemini、Cursor、Aider 等），用你自己的订阅或 API Key。 可以通过 o8 命令行或任何 MCP 客户端使用。 macOS 14+ 提供签名、自动更新的安装包；Linux 有预览版安装包（AppImage、DEB、RPM）。 目前的进度：审查、退回修改、复审已经在主分支可用；统一的受控合并和按项目规则自动合并还在开发中，路线图在仓库的 ROADMAP.md。欢迎反馈。

projects.title: Show HN: Yet another agent manager (but we needed it)
projects.author: imakris
projects.summary: Hello HN, I am Ioannis and I would like to introduce Logonomic, a desktop application we made to help us work with LLM CLIs (e.g. codex, claude, opencode etc) in a more organized way. It runs the CLIs already installed, with their existing accounts and configuration and organizes sessions by repository. It is available for Windows and Linux, with a preview for macOS. There is also a mobile companion app, to work remotely (Android and soon iOS too). We built it originally to assist us in our own work, to address the common case of multiple agents running concurrently in many repositories. It was hard to keep track of what each one is doing and which one needs attention or requires action. There are many tools by now broadly that broadly target the same problem. This one is a native C++/Qt application with our own terminal emulator. Some of its features: - An 'overview' mode that shows all running sessions, optionally grouped by repository, each with its status, title and summary that the agents update regularly. - Agents add a trailer to their commits, enabling to re-open the conversations that produced them. - Terminals run in their own processes and survive UI crashes. - A plot that shows line counts over time, by directory or language, where clicking on a sample brings up the corresponding commit in the git log. - A treemap that shows how the repo's files are organized, with a diff mode that colours changed files, whose diff opens with a double click. - Token usage and remaining account quotas shown where available, with usage broken down by day and repository. - Sessions can exchange messages (1:1 or broadcast), may hand tasks to each other or continue other session's work. The supported CLIs are Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, Antigravity, Grok Build, Kimi Code and Qwen Code. The free edition has no time limit and runs up to four terminals. The paid editions have perpetual one-time licences from €150 for 2 seats and include 12 months of feature updates, no terminal limit, GitHub/GitLab CI integrations, as well as an Android companion app (iOS will follow). The application itself is proprietary. Many of its core components are open source, among them the terminal emulator and the plotting library: https://github.com/Varinomics This is the first public release, so there will be rough edges, and we would like to hear about them.

projects.author: pmkelly4444
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm working on a context layer built on OSS and open standards that lets agents search your company knowledge and use MCP tools all through a single gateway with code mode. Building this because we believe context can and should be portable across harnesses. The metric we are solving for here is "cost to resolution". Given any question or a task, how quickly and cheaply can we put an agent on the correct path. Tech behind that: 1. Context map: software to create and maintain a context map of people, teams, systems, relationships, etc. It's built on OKF, import/export from this open standard. 2. Code mode: agents explore the map with a token efficient context eng. method (open source runtime, find portofcontext/pctx on GitHub) 3. Indexing: Hybrid keyword and semantic search on any unstructured text, with code mode on top (we will open source this part soon, although it's nothing special, the interesting part is placing content in the map and putting code mode on it) Some proof that it works: 1. Goose + code mode: https://aaif.io/blog/how-port-of-context-eliminated-producti... 2. tau-bench: https://portofcontext.com/blog/context-layer-platform-benchm... With Port of Context To try it, paste this into your coding agent: Set up pctx.ai/onboard.md It will help you create an account, scan your active MCP connections, and help configure the gateway. Hope you find this useful and feel free to reach out: patrick@portofcontext.com

projects.author: harshkrjha
projects.summary: Hey HN! I am Harsh, been developing software for quite sometime now. Since agents came into my local SD workflow I had been facing a bottleneck. Event though agents are great in working parallelly, testing their changes and iterating is a pain. (Brain, storage & memory overhead) We all use Git worktrees to code in parallel. But how do we test those changes? Still linearly. Or patched up multi-environment setup. And what if you have multiple microservices in an application? How do you test different combinations? I am building Headwig to help me with this. It lets me run multiple agents on my app, isolate their changes across services, and test and iterate on each one independently, even while other agents are working, without the storage overhead of duplicating workspaces for every task. I've been using it for my own webapp, and I want you guys to look at the workflow and see if it makes sense and give me any suggestions or feedback. https://harsh-kr-jha.github.io/headwig/

projects.title: Show HN: Agent-plan a CLI that automatically commits your agent's plans
projects.author: ghmeier
projects.summary: After spending quite a bit of time using various coding agents and a workflow that uses markdown-based research/plan/handoff documents to hold context across sessions, I kept on running into an this question of how and where to store the generated markdown. The contents are usually useful for posterity and future projects in the same feature area. However, it felt burdensome for myself or reviewers to clutter up diffs with largeish markdown documents. This left me with a mess of uncommitted markdown and a waste of tokens having LLMs collate the documentation. I figured this was the perfect usecase for a small CLI tool and some hooks that automatically create and sync planning documentation for the team. That's how agent-plan got started. It uses an orphan git branch a worktree checkout and symlinks to keep all the planning files available from any branch. There's a claude and codex plugin that install a couple hooks to sync and commit any edits as they happen. Myself and my team have been using this for the last month or so, and have found that it really smooths out document-driven development. It's straightforward to hand off plans between people, and easy to reference all the older documentation. It also solves a small (but frequent) papercut I had where I'd have to remember file names to reference them in subsequent chats. Since agent-plan stores everything in consistent formatting with some added frontmatter metadata, it's really easily searchable with plain text search. I figure lots of teams might have a similar sort of problem and I could save you some time.

projects.title: Show HN: AI-drop project – drop traffic fast from misbehaving crawlers (AGPL)
projects.author: catab
projects.summary: Hello! All started with 4 million requests / day on rocketgit.com (AGPL git hosting). Instead of thousands. Enough is enough! Presentation (8 pages): https://rocketgit.com/user/catalinux/ai-drop/artefacts/downl... So, I built AI-drop free-software project (AGPL) to block this kind of crawlers. rocketgit.com has a very restrictive robots.txt (only around 10 pages are allowed). But the crawlers are not respecting it. So, who is not respecting it will be blocked. Limiting by IP or user-agent is not working anymore. The crawlers are using millions of IPs and it takes days to reuse an IP. And they use fake user-agents. I am using honeypots to build a list of misbehaving IPs which are streamed to downstream instances. Right now I have around 1.573.000 IPv4 and 6.000 IPv6 misbehaving addresses. I keep them in the list only for 7 days to not block somebody legit. I am watching the traffic on rocketgit.com and the solution is working nicely. It uses an eBPF program to fast drop the packets. You can try it easily on your Linux servers: # Check https://rocketgit.com/user/catalinux/ai-drop/pkg # If your distribution is already there, follow the instructions. # It is the best way to keep you up-to-date. # Look inside 'ai-drop.spec' or 'debian/control' and install the dependencies. git clone https://rocketgit.com/user/catalinux/ai-drop cd ai-drop ./configure make install # edit /etc/ai-drop.conf # Very important: # set 'interface' (non 'eth' are not supported now) # set 'safe_mode = 0' if you only want to evaluate the product. Then: systemctl enable --now ai-drop journalctl -f -u ai-drop # The list of misbehaving IPs will be streamed from the main server. # Look at the statistics, especially 'drops': ai-drop dump-stats # Output example: # now=1794482762 ipv4_total=0 ipv6_total=0 total=0 \ # ipv4_adds=0 ipv6_adds=0 adds=0 \ # ipv4_updates=0 ipv6_updates=0 updates=0 \ # ipv4_drops=0 ipv6_drops=0 drops=0 \ # ipv4_real_drops=0 ipv6_real_drops=0 real_drops=0 \ # ipv4_expires=0 ipv6_expires=0 expires=0 \ # ipv4_deletes=0 ipv6_deletes=0 deletes=0 \ # last_load=0 daemon_start=0 Please note that no AI was used to build this software. Thank you for your time! Catalin(ux) C.M.T. BOIE

projects.title: 开源了 Browser Hands：让 Codex/Cursor 也能用上 Claude 官方插件级浏览器操作
projects.author: Thor88
projects.summary: 平时重度用 Claude Code 、Codex 还有 Hermes 、OpenClaw 这类 Agent 干活，经常需要让它们帮忙在网页上填表、点后台、查资料。但浏览器控制这块一直用得很憋屈，折腾了几个周末，干脆自己写了个开源工具叫 **Browser Hands**，今天发出来给大伙试用。 **演示（ 20 秒）**：Agent 在我已登录的 Chrome 里自动填 Product Hunt 的提交表单 ![Browser Hands 演示]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/214140846/browser-hands/main/docs/media/demo.gif) **它是什么** 简单说，就是一个 Chrome 扩展 + 一个本地运行的 MCP Server （打包完就一个 450 KB 左右的单文件 JS ）。不需要起云端 VM ，也不用开无头浏览器，直接让任何支持 MCP 的 Agent 接管你平时正在用的 Chrome——点击、输入、读页面、截图、跑 JS 、录 GIF 都行。 **为什么不用现成的方案？** 做之前把市面上的方案基本试了一圈，各有各的难受： 1. **Claude / Codex 官方 Chrome 插件**：体验确实顶，但绑定了单一厂商和订阅。我平时同时用 Codex 、Cursor 、Hermes 、WorkBuddy ，这些 Agent 根本享受不到同等待遇。而且官方插件内置权限限制太多，跑个流程动不动就弹窗让你确认，效率全卡在人工点按钮上。 2. **Playwright / Chrome DevTools MCP 这类工具**：每次新起一个干净的浏览器实例，没有我现成的 Cookie 和登录态；连接经常莫名其妙断开；运行的时候还会抢窗口焦点，动不动触发风控验证。 3. **ego**：试过一阵，资源占用偏高，开几个任务电脑就开始发热风扇狂转。 **Browser Hands 解决了什么问题** * **多 Agent 并行不打架**：每个 Agent 会话会分配独立的 Chrome 标签组（ Tab Group ），各自只能看到和操作自己组里的标签页，多开并行互不干扰。也支持自定义标签组。 * **多 Google Profile 切换**：像我平时工作号和个人号是分开两个 Chrome Profile 的，Agent 能直接识别每个 Profile 的名称和邮箱，切换很稳。 * **省 Token 且不发热**：页面读取优先走无障碍树（ Accessibility Tree ）和纯文本，必要时才截图；截图直接走 Chrome DevTools Protocol 底层缩放，不在页面里跑 Canvas 渲染。我自己在 Mac 上开很多标签页跑任务，CPU 占用很低，本子基本不怎么烫。 * **内置快速小模型路由（ quick_task ）**：遇到纯机械的点击路径，可以通过 `quick_task` 交给小模型（ JEV ）去跑，单步决策大概 0.2 到 0.5 秒，省主模型 Token 也省时间。同时内置了 `stopBefore` 机制，遇到 Submit 、Pay 、Delete 这类关键按钮会硬性卡住等你确认（这个功能需要配 Typesafe 或 OpenRouter 的 Key ，其他所有基础功能零配置开箱即用）。 * **Prompt 零成本迁移**：一共 26 个工具接口，其中 16 个的参数和命名直接对齐了 Claude in Chrome ，原来的提示词基本不用改就能直接用。 **三步安装** 1. 终端跑一行 `curl | sh` 安装脚本（如果本地装了 `claude` CLI ，会自动帮你把 MCP 配置注册进 Claude Code ）。 2. 打开 Chrome 扩展管理页，开启开发者模式，“加载已解压的扩展程序”选中扩展目录。 3. 其他客户端（ Cursor / Codex 等）把本地 MCP 配置贴进去就能连上。 **目前的不足（先打个预防针）** * 目前只适配了 **macOS**（需要 Node 18+ 和 Chrome ）。 * 业余时间单人维护，刚开源出来，目前还没来得及整理严格的量化跑分数据，上面的体验描述全基于我自己的日常重度使用。 项目采用 MIT 协议开源，现在仓库里才 8 个 Star ，冷启动阶段非常需要大家帮忙踩踩坑。如果觉得思路还行，欢迎去点个 Star 或者提 Issue 吐槽： GitHub: https://github.com/214140846/browser-hands

projects.title: Show HN: Langfuse AI Gateway, open source rust gateway to trace every LLM call
projects.author: clemo_ra
projects.summary: Hi HN, this is Max, Marc and Clemens, co-founders of Langfuse, the open source tool for agent & observability & evals ( https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse ). It’s been a minute since our last Show HN in August 2023 ( https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=37310070 ) - we’ve been busy building out and serving our tracing & eval pieces over the past years and have been very lucky to build a successful company and open source project around it. Today, we are happy to show the beta of Langfuse AI Gateway: https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/tree/main/ai-gateway . You may ask, why an AI Gateway as our second product: it’s been one our community’s strongest asks + integration pattern that we’ve seen. We want to offer a scalable, reliable and secure way to solve for the gateway use case in the same way that we’ve done with tracing/evals over the past years. And we’ve recently grown our team with some excellent folks - expect to see more bigger bets from us. Our observability SDKs currently see the code you instrument. Much of a company's model traffic runs through code that is not or cannot be easily instrumented: coding agents like Pi, Claude Code and Codex, internal tools, scripts etc. Third party gateways are already popular ways to emit traces to Langfuse and we’re happy to now ship one natively. You change your base URL and your API key. Langfuse AI Gateway forwards the native request with a provider key that does not need to be distributed across the team. Right now, it doesn't translate between APIs, responses are relayed unchanged. This was a conscious decision to ensure stability for gateway users, as translation between e.g. OpenAI responses and Anthropic messages are imperfect and might lead to subtle failures in your agents. If you pass a traceparent header, the call lands inside your existing Langfuse traces. You can try by docker composing langfuse up and then on to http://localhost:3000 -- git clone https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse.git cd langfuse docker compose up -- On Cloud, each call becomes a Langfuse generation with tokens, cost, latency and time to first token. Prompts and outputs are recorded if you opt in. If you self-hosted you can also track nothing, not even metadata. Some details: - Written in Rust. Stateless, with no database; it talks only to the Langfuse platform and the providers. - 22MB Docker image. Under 3ms median overhead with tracing on, 1,000+ concurrent streams on 2 vCPUs. - MIT licensed. Self-host it with Docker Compose or Helm or use our Cloud version. - Your provider keys and contracts. We don't resell tokens. What’s next? - Budget caps per key, user, team - Custom model aliases and fallbacks - Guardrails - PII redaction - SCIM user provisioning We’ll be around & looking forward to all questions & comments

projects.title: Show HN: Deccy – software engineering as decision management
projects.author: nelaggy
projects.summary: Hi HN, We built deccy out of frustration from working with coding agents. Although we love the speed that AI has brought to our work, we also want to have control over what we build. While it's not impossible to keep up with the changes AI makes, it is significantly more difficult when compared to writing code ourselves. We realised that what we cared about most was not controlling every line of the implementation, but preserving our intent (we especially hated when agents would wrongly guess what we wanted). We iterated through planning and spec-driven methods, but found that both writing our own plans/specifications and reading AI-generated versions was tedious and exhausting. Eventually, we decided to split the specifications up into the decisions that make them up, and get agents to do the boring work of tracking and bookkeeping. deccy is the first realisation of this idea. We're already working on the next iteration, but we wanted to share the mental model we developed. There's a long way to go from here, and we'd really love any feedback :)

projects.title: Show HN: ReadyStack.dev – Bit-for-bit reproducible OSS containers
projects.author: readystack
projects.summary: https://readystack.dev If you are like me, coding LLMs made open source more important not less. A few months ago I wanted to see how far I could get using minimal LLM cost (local on two 3090s and one subscription) to automate OSS containers with a build recipe that matched bits. That project ended up as ReadyStack.dev. ReadyStack publishes free Community Edition containers for open-source applications. I designed it to be a low cost image standard that puts provenance as a first order concern. My goal was to see if I could build in trust with my images in a way nobody else had. Use the build recipe and match bits. Each release's build kit includes everything the build needs: upstream source pinned, the OS packages as .debs, the language dependencies, the base images saved by digest, fixed SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH. BUILD_OFFLINE.sh rebuilds with the network off, so mirrors dropping old packages don't matter, and VERIFY_OFFLINE.sh checks your digest against ours. We currently have 101 of 101 releases reproducing their published linux/amd64 digest in our clean-room rebuild process, which is just a trust signal, but an important one as we don't have much of, if at all. Certainly, not for free. For full disclosure, I built a sister project, ce.rodeo, which grades container images from all publishers, including ReadyStack.dev. Yes, it is a conflict of interest to grade my own images. I publish the measuring criteria and I needed a standard of what existed so I had to create a grading system first. Happy to hear suggestions. I started out to do something for OSS. I designed it to run on a skinny budget and it is doing that. It runs on donations, so far just mine. The bigger idea is that open-source software should be having its greatest era now that everyone has a DevOps genius at their fingertips. I chose to take a leap and build a platform to be part of that. Happy to answer questions.

projects.title: Show HN: Cerulion – ROS 2-compatible robotics runtime with multi-process replay
projects.author: lakshays

github.name: cerulion-inc/cerulion
github.description: Cerulion (YC S24) gives AI agents a harness to control real robots. Our open-source runtime and harness give any AI agent a physical body, inside safety limits the robot enforces, and tools to autonomously debug recorded robot failures. It's ROS 2 compatible.

projects.summary: Hey HN! I'm Lakshay. Raveen and I have built Cerulion, a ROS2-compatible robotics runtime written in Rust. We've worked hard on lowering IPC transport latencies without making the single process tradeoff or forcing POD message types. These fast multi-process graphs can then be resimmed deterministically, and existing ROS2 nodes/launch files can run unmodified alongside native Cerulion Rust/Python code. Installation and quickstart (with a one-shot prompt for your favorite coding agent) here at the repo README: https://github.com/cerulion-inc/cerulion I worked on off-road autonomy during my PhD at MIT, and we kept running into inter-process latency in ROS (2 lidars and 6 cameras). Loaned messages need POD types, which nukes standard, vendor-agnostic Image/PointCloud2. We ended up running some hot paths in a brittle single process, which made debugging a nightmare. I'm sure you've seen the heisenbugs ROS-based stacks can produce, with no way to easily reproduce the consumption order or interleaving of callbacks. Valuable data of runtime failures on the robot was hard to use effectively without deterministic reproducibility. This is what we fix. Cerulion bags record per-input reads and scheduler traces alongside message content in standard MCAPs. cerulion bag play --resim all --verify re-executes node code on the recorded schedule and compares each byte for exact matches or within defined tolerances. Exit 0 is a match, 1 shows the first topic/frame that diverges, 6 shows schedule divergence and --report gives an optional CI verdict. Eligible ROS2 processes can replay deterministically as well. Here's the data loop: 1. Run: Dependency-ordered level-based DAG scheduler with periodic/data/sync triggers, I/O deadlines, backpressure, and automatic profiling for process partitioning. Each node by default free-runs in its own process while preserving deterministic replay. Live runs pause/resume, and UMWAIT/WFE parks idle consumers on CPUs that support it. Wall-clock reads and runtime thread spawns in user code rejected at compile time by macros. ROS 2 is supported with rmw_cerulion for Foxy, Humble, Jazzy and Lyrical, that lets you run ROS2 nodes/launch files unmodified in the same graph as native Cerulion nodes. LD_PRELOAD gives ROS2 code shared memory loans through std::vector/std::string. cerulion ros2 attach folds in already-running ROS2 robots, and cerulion ros2 run/launch lets you run existing ROS2 workspaces on Cerulion without any additional setup (with an optional automatic migrate suggested that rewrites C++ publish sites). 2. Move: iceoryx2 shared memory with no serialization, no payload copy and no payload-sized allocation, including for variable-length messages like sensor_msgs/Image and PointCloud2. Round trip latency for a 1MiB sensor_msgs/Image between two processes is 4.08µs p50, with a tight tail of 7.38µs p99 (under 2x p50), with recording on . This is default Cerulion, against 10.95 ms for default ROS 2 Jazzy. Cerulion's p50 and p99 stay flat from 64B to 16 MiB. 3. Capture: With this round-trip latency, there are no tradeoffs, not for process isolation and not for bagging. We can afford always-on or event-based logging. Flashback is our robot dashcam: keeps ~30s of all logs and message contents in memory and saves it automatically on process crashes, topic stalls or declared incidents/manual triggers. 4. Reach: A free account lets you pair robots and desks, letting all your devices find each other with no config, IP addresses or discovery chatter. Pubsub is authenticated and on-demand, with signed grants that the robot verifies offline. We use Iroh to hole-punch or relay over WAN, and mDNS over LAN to transmit data using QUIC. Remote topics mirror into local shared memory, and each device has a single network gateway. 5. Diagnose: cerulion doctor scans for compile/run-time issues (better than Windows Troubleshooter I promise) and suggests fixes. Hindsight is an early access MCP to let agents analyze your bags. To get started: go to the repo, install Cerulion with the curl one-liner, and paste the prompt in Claude Code/Codex: https://github.com/cerulion-inc/cerulion#quickstart-run-reco... . Or shift your own gears, it's all in the repo that you should star! The CLI needs a free account, which we use to make device pairing as easy as AirDrop USED to be ;) Everything runs on Linux (x86_64/ARM64), macOS and Android (JNI), with more platforms coming. We'd love to hear your feedback! If you run ROS 2 on a real robot, point this at your stack and tell us what breaks. Docs: https://docs.cerulion.com Site: https://cerulion.com

projects.title: Show HN: Wonderchat – A Zendesk alternative that doesn't charge per seat
projects.author: walkingsunrise
projects.summary: Hi HN, I’m Vera, co-founder of Wonderchat. We started as an AI website agent that answers customer questions from a company’s website and docs. Over time, customers kept asking for the rest of the support stack around it, so we built a helpdesk: live chat, a unified inbox for email and SMS, and a help center (coming soon in a couple of weeks). The pricing and AI native helpdesk experience is the part I most wanted to change. Most helpdesks charge per seat, so every new teammate adds to the bill, and support teams end up rationing logins. We charge one flat price with unlimited seats. You pay only for AI work: the replies and resolutions the agent handles. Human agents replying to tickets don’t cost anything extra. We've also rebuilt the entire customer service helpdesk around the ideas of AI agent deflecting frontline support tickets first, and having an AI helpdesk agent that helps to draft auto replies to incoming tickets. As the human agent approves its responses and sends them out, the AI helpdesk agent learns about the internal support SOPs to then continually draft better AI responses. The product is built for users to self-serve their customer service operations set up. You don’t have to open our dashboard to set it up. Open your site’s code in Claude Code, Cursor or any coding agent and paste: “Follow https://app.wonderchat.io/llms.txt to add a Wonderchat AI support agent to this site. Train it on [your website], test it with a few real customer questions, and add the chat widget to the shared layout.” A few technical details: AI answers come from our own retrieval engine, built for large and messy knowledge bases (we have customers with 10,000+ documents) You can pick which AI model the agent runs on, so you aren’t locked into one provider It’s still early. Helpcenter is still a build in progress. You can try it free at https://wonderchat.io/ , no credit card needed. I’d especially like feedback on the product, pricing model, and from anyone who is considering a customer service agent and ticketing software, what made you decide on Zendesk/Intercom? What would make you do the switch?

projects.summary: Hey hn, i'm Armel solo dev from Abidjan. I built upstar a github trending like website where projects are ranked by how fast they grow in each topic I love discovering new projects, so I spend a lot of my time scrolling Reddit and X. I thought, why not get the trending projects I care about in my inbox, like I already get good articles from Medium? I looked at GitHub Trending, but it mostly shows big projects. It's hard to find small projects that also deserve attention. So I built this tool. There are 69 topics, from programming languages to subjects like agent skills, reverse engineering, emulation, etc. The score is the stars gained in the current period (day, week or month) divided by the square root of the stars the project had before that period. So small projects can rank above big projects, even if the big ones gain more stars. I try my best to keep malicious projects out without penalizing good small legit projects. Each project is analyzed by judges (Claude Haiku, Sonnet and Opus) that follow rules I set. Two weeks ago I reported a malware campaign of 479 repos to GitHub, and most of the accounts behind it are gone now. This week I found 333 more that sent people to installers outside GitHub. You can browse the site freely, with no ads and no tracking. To get the Monday digest for the topics you choose, you sign in with GitHub, or just leave your email. There's also an MCP server, for people who prefer to ask their AI agent directly. I built the project with the help of Claude Code, and the short repo summaries are written by AI. The hardest part was putting projects in the right topics. That's why I'd love your feedback on the rankings and the topics, if any of this speaks to you.

projects.title: Show HN: Klad, a paint app your coding agent can drive (source-available)
projects.author: ambewas

github.name: klad-app/klad
github.description: A drawing app built for agent/human collaboration

projects.summary: I've been developing applications for a long time and have turned to game development as well lately. One of the things that frustrated me the most was that using AI agents for game development is very annoying in the art department. Your only options right now are to either use an image genAI model and roll the dice every time you want to make an edit, or have your agent draw with something like vectors. I was looking for an application that would allow me to ask an agent to make a first draft of whatever art I needed with actual brushes, and then be able to go in myself and edit every last stroke or layer that it created. Klad is that application. Written in Rust, it can be fully controlled by an agent through the CLI, and every function is available in a nice UI as well: a brush engine, frame-by-frame animation (and bones/IK), vectors, text layers, colours, layer effects, infinite undo (even after re-opening the file!),… Why I think it's useful for a wider audience: Adobe showed agents editing Photoshop files at MAX this week, with a private beta planned for early 2027. Klad is built on the same core idea, with editable paint strokes as core architecture, and it works today. Clone the repo to try it out: https://github.com/klad-app/klad You can basically point Claude to the repo, ask it to build it, and pick up the drawing skills. Then ask it to make any drawing you want! (After that, you or the agent can change absolutely every brush stroke in the app again, which makes edits a breeze.) The quality of the drawings really depends on the agent you use. I have tried it with Claude Fable 5.2 since it came out on Monday, and the drawings are already quite impressive. I'm confident that this will only improve. I use it every day on Mac, so that definitely works well. It builds on Linux too (tablet pen pressure still needs some work there). Windows builds in CI, I haven't used it there myself yet but I have some reports that it works perfectly fine. Coming up next is support for pixel art. I'm in the testing phase with this right now, and I expect it to go live in the repo sometime this weekend. Klad is source-available rather than open source: free to build and use for individuals and small companies, and I plan to sell pre-built binaries later, the way Aseprite does. The file format, CLI reference and agent skill are MIT. What I want to hear from people who try it: Can your agent work out the CLI without help, and where does it get confused? Can you go in and change one of its strokes easily? The command reference and guides are available at https://klad.studio I'll be here answering any questions about the technical side as well, as it's a pretty interesting challenge to build a performant engine with editable brush strokes that render as paint.

projects.summary: I was finding that managing multiple agent threads with walls of text was getting tiring and inefficient for me and that I wanted a more visual way to interact with my agents, so I built Lynx. Lynx lets you quickly build fully custom interfaces connected to your data sources (e.g. via MCP or API) and trigger agents running on your machine from them (e.g. with Claude Code or Codex). I built it as an experiment but have found myself doing 80-90% of my work from inside Lynx. I have my own Conductor-like workspace for coding, a Mail client, a workspace for my writing, and various others for dashboards and explorations. A few things are really cool about it: - Adding buttons to a UI that trigger a Claude Code agent running on my machine (e.g. to review a PR, get started on a task from Linear, or look for typos in my text) - Iterating on the interfaces is really easy, particularly because of a point tool that let's you select what you want changed and an agent will update it live - Switching between workspaces takes a fraction of a second (much faster than e.g. switching between websites) - It's all local :) Harnesses have been moving towards native support for artifacts and MCP-UI which kind of go in this direction but I think the current models add to context fragmentation rather than actually help it, so I flipped the model on its head and built an AI workspace / harness where interactive interfaces are at the core. Calling this an AI workspace for now but honestly unsure what the proper term should be. Is this a visual harness? A hub for personal software? projects.summary: I'm new here, and little nervous about posting, but here goes. I'm not a newbie. I started programming in BASIC when my dad bought home a TRS-80 Model I in 1980, when I was 16. Other than a 9-year stint as active duty military, I've spent 46 years either personally or professionally working in tech. I've programmed in RPG using punch cards for an IBM /System360, and COBOL on a DEC pdp 11/34. I've worked professionally with VB, C#, SQL Server, ColdFusion, PHP, and more. I've seen a lot of technologies come and go. So this ain't the first time I've jogged around this track. Here's the problem I wanted to solve: I hate WordPress. I mean, as a concept, it's fine, but I used to have a fairly popular motorcycle blog on WP that got trashed by hackers. I've also run into that problem with customers. When hackers find a wordpress site, they just bang on it like a drum. It's a pain. It's also a pain just to manage it, with a wild-west plugin system where plugins constantly fall in and out of compatibility. I'm also not a huge fan of PHP, but since it comes stock with pretty much every shared hosting service, where a lot of my web work is done, it's kind of the default for doing web stuff. Back in about 2006 or so, I built my own blogging software, which I called .Blog, as an ASP.NET deal in C#. It took me about 6 months to build, start to finish. I didn't have time to keep up with it, which is why I defaulted back to WP sometime around 2014. I migrated to Grav when I ran across it (I guess around 2020 or so), and I liked that. But Grav ran into some issues, and development on it really slowed. In the past year or so, the company I work for has been delving into using Claude Code, and I got an idea. What if I could just use Claude Code to build a CMS that has everything I want, and nothing I don't? This project is the result of that idea. I designed the specifications for what I wanted it to do, and let Claude Code handle the actual code writing. I started with a flat-file, markdown-based flat-file CMS, and iterated on that. Fiddling around with markdown files and folders started to get tedious, so I moved towards SQLite as the back-end, to create a system as self-contained and easy to use as possible. This project is, I think, the final result of that idea. This project, from start to finish, took about 2 weeks to build using Laravel/Filament/PHP with Claude Code, compared to the 6 months it took to build .Blog by hand, 20 years ago. Cripes, I'm old. Personally, I'm pretty pleased with how this project turned out. I'm running two public websites on it. I'd be interested to hear what others think.

projects.title: Show HN: Bot-bottle – secure runtime, DLP and remote control for local agents
projects.author: didericis
projects.summary: Hey! About 6 months ago, I started looking for a tool to safely run coding agents on my (security sensitive) developer machine. Specifically, I wanted a tool that: - I could use regardless of the model or harness running underneath - I could build simple, composable, plaintext security policies for - Provided strong vm level isolation - Hid credentials from agents - Scanned and monitored everything going in and out of agent workspace - Allowed me to use the same mobile flow I had gotten used to with claude code, but with arbitrary harnesses I couldn't find a tool that met all of these, so I started bot-bottle. It's evolved into what I'm hoping will be the best security conscious, local first coding agent orchestrator out there. Here's how it works: Each agent runs in its own microVM (Firecracker on Linux, Apple's container on macOS, Docker as a weaker fallback), with whichever harness you want. Claude Code, Codex and pi are built in, and custom agent providers are supported (still being documented/tested). What an agent can reach is defined in a "bottle", which is just a short markdown file listing hosts, repos and which secret goes to which host. Bottles are enforced by a gateway outside the agent VM, which adds the real credentials to requests on the way out, so the agent only sees placeholders. Bottles stack, so you can keep small ones around (npm read only, one repo, one API, etc) and combine them per task. Repos can ship their own bottles, which only run after you trust their exact contents. Outgoing requests and git pushes are scanned for secrets, and everything is logged locally (you can stream it to your own endpoint as NDJSON or OCSF). Anything a bottle doesn't allow comes to you for approval, in the terminal or on your phone through an optional paired console. It's in alpha (the console especially), so UI polish is still in progress. Install: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/diderisoft/bot-bottle/main/install.sh | sh Docs: https://bot-bottle.com/docs Would love feedback, especially on the threat model and on whether bottles are the right abstraction.

projects.title: 写了个本地安全提取 ChatGPT Account ID 的油猴脚本，避免直接复制 /api/auth/session 泄露完整 Token
projects.author: liuyao729
projects.summary: 身边有朋友在处理 ChatGPT 订阅异常或者核对账户标识时，习惯直接打开 `chatgpt.com/api/auth/session` 把整个页面返回的 JSON 复制出去。 看过这个接口返回结构的应该都知道，最底部直接明文带着当前会话的 `accessToken`（JWT 格式）。只要在有效期内，拿到这个字段就等同于拿到了完整的登录态，可以绕过密码和 2FA 直接调接口或操作账户。 实际上用来区分账户归属的只是 `account.id` 字段（UUID 格式的 Account ID，本身不包含鉴权凭据）。为了避免手动复制 JSON 时不小心把底部的 `accessToken` 一起粘出去，我写了个简单的 Tampermonkey 油猴脚本，只在本地浏览器同源请求并提取 `account.id`。 ### 1. 临时用：控制台单行命令 如果只是偶尔查一次，不想装脚本，登录 `chatgpt.com` 后按 F12 在 Console 跑这一行就行： ~~~javascript fetch('/api/auth/session').then(r=>r.json()).then(s=>console.log('Account ID:', s?.account?.id || '未找到')) ~~~ ### 2. 常驻用：Tampermonkey 油猴脚本 如果平时需要频繁核对多账号或者排查订阅状态，可以直接用仓库里的 `tools/get-account-id.user.js`。 脚本逻辑很简单（总共 50 多行纯原生 JS，无外部依赖）： - 仅在 `chatgpt.com` 域名下注册油猴菜单项 `查询 Account ID（本地）` - 点击后同源读取 `/api/auth/session` 并解析 `account.id` - 弹窗仅展示脱敏后的 Account ID 供手动复制，不会读取或上传任何 Cookie 与 Token 另外在 `tools/check_connection.py` 里顺手放了个零依赖的 Python 小脚本，用来在终端快速测试相关公开页面的 HTTP 状态码、响应耗时与超时排查。 ### 3. 附带的 Codex 与订阅排查文档 最近 OpenAI 调整了 Plus、Pro 各档位的额度策略，加上不少人在终端用 Codex CLI（Sign in with ChatGPT 模式 vs API Key 模式）时经常遇到额度扣减异常或者已扣款仍显示 Free 的问题，我把 2026 最新的套餐对比、Codex 额度计算规则、银行卡拒付（AVS/卡段风控）排查整理在了同一个仓库里。 - GitHub 仓库： https://github.com/zhaozhao010/chatgpt-pluspro-tutorial - 脚本工具目录： https://github.com/zhaozhao010/chatgpt-pluspro-tutorial/tree/main/tools 代码和文档都很简单，主要图个安全省事。如果对大家有用欢迎点个 Star，文档里有出入的地方也欢迎提 Issue 补充。

projects.title: three.dev
projects.summary: Almost every team now runs AI in production, but few know how it behaves once real users show up. The failures are quiet: a wrong refund policy, a made-up order status. Nothing crashes, so you hear about it from your users. three.dev finds those failures in your live traffic on its own and ranks them by severity. Setup is one prompt to Claude Code, Cursor, or Codex. Then your coding agent gets what it needs to write the fix.

projects.title: Changeset
projects.summary: For anyone doing a code project: Intentional software engineering, human-in-the-loop. You don’t want your codebase turning into a pile of slop that no one can understand and maintain. You want to get back to software that endures, not software that's disposable. Create notes for ideas, backlog items, issues, and improvements. These notes become conversation threads between you and your coding agent. Learn more at https://changeset.appuniversa.com/changeset Changeset is a desktop app.

projects.title: Vibecoder Zone
projects.summary: Vibecoder Zone is an online catalog for finding the perfect AI-coding stack. It lists 624 tools across 36 categories, including AI coding assistants, LLM APIs, deployment, databases, auth, payments, AI search, image/video generation and workflow automation, plus curated stacks, leaderboards and price comparisons.

projects.title: ApiTraffic
projects.summary: ApiTraffic records every request your Node.js API handles: the payload, the database queries behind it and the firewall's verdict. It alerts you when an endpoint breaks, drifts or slows down after a deploy, flags N+1 queries down to the file and line, and blocks bad bots and risky outbound calls inside your app. Redaction runs in your process, so sensitive data never leaves your network. Every failure becomes a paste-ready fix for your AI coding agent.

projects.title: CyteEditor
projects.summary: A rich text editor SDK for apps that handle real documents. Word paste keeps structure, snapshots diff at block level, auto format fixes quotes, spacing and numbering. Six framework adapters and a free Community tier.

projects.title: 我用 10 天，把 Super-agent 架构做成了一个 7×24 小时在线的产品
projects.author: nifengfei
projects.summary: 10 月 31 日，DeepSeek Harness 团队发表了《Super-agent 设计探索：迈向更自主的 Agent 系统》，读完以后我就做了个决定，要将它实现落地。10 天过去了，今晚我让刚上线的 Fable5.2 测完最后一个用例后，就正式上线了。 这是一个真正的 7*24 小时持久在线的 Super-agent，存算分离，云端 Loop 与重状态的环境解耦，水平可扩展，基本实现了文中说的架构和功能。同时是一个 SaaS 产品。 ### 1.为什么第一眼就决定要将它实现落地？ 因为我自己就是文中的「人肉 Router」，harness 和模型能力的提升使得我们不必再困于具体繁琐的工作，而是转向了更多任务的分配和决策，目标的验收。 回顾我的工作日常，基本上是同时开五六个项目，平均每个项目开 3-5 个 session，终端也从传统的 terminal 换成了支持无限拓展和布局的新型终端，一般还会辅助 Cursor 再开两 2 个 session，用来偶尔瞄几眼代码。大概是下面这样子，隐藏掉了项目的细节： ![]( https://i.v2ex.co/12D7WII5.png) 新终端效率很高，我偶尔看看 session 细节，和模型要我做的决定，更多是要在一个窗口启动服务器，另外一个窗口派任务，再来一个跑测试，还有一个询问项目细节，再来一个上网调研资料...然后模型没额度了，换个桌面版 agent，使用一下 Browser use，还有各个渠道来的信息。 我同时驱动很多 session 并行工作，我有任务目标，有一致的上下文，我在电脑桌前坐很久，我也希望换个沙发，躺下来用语音发命令。 Super-agent 这套架构看了一遍，基本觉得落地没问题，不是因为“工程问题很简单”，而是因为在我们只有痛苦和抱怨的时候，它已经将答案递到了我们面前，我觉得这绝对算**探索未至之境**。 我相信作者也是在经历了上述种种痛苦以后，再加上一个很小的产品试验，也就是「公共群聊中产品问题，到开发，到 pull request 提交」的一条链路，以小见大，加之计算机和行业知识的积累，才有了这份架构设计。这个设计基本就是量身定做的，同时将本地 Coding Agent 组合，然后搬到线上是我一直的想法。 ### 2.先从架构学习入手 文章认为 Super-Agent(简写 SA)具备下面四个特征： - **连续**：文中说的「连续」是围绕 Agent 在说的，它应该出现在它需要工作的所有地方。因为人是通过不同渠道和工具获取工作信息的，需要将 Agent 的上下文拉到同一个层次，而不是手动去维护这些。接入各个信息渠道，并共享上下文是关键。 - **高效**：信息和任务是并发来的，所以工作也应该并行执行，一个独立的任务不应该等待。这需要独立的，互不干扰的工作环境。 - **主动**：无需用户参与，持续观察环境并主动推进。这种是由于事件驱动的，触发 SA 的相应。其实还有一种 schedule 触发，按照时间规划来执行一些任务，时间间隔短一些，也可以有非常主动、聪明积极的感觉，并不是简单的定时任务。 - **持久**：也就是一些自我修复的机制。这样持续在线的 SA，一直有人帮忙清理异常，才能持续高效工作。 ![]( https://i.v2ex.co/BKEFFGAM.png) 围绕着这四大特征，设计了 5 个系统，这里重点讲一下「Router 层的双层架构」，并对它进行扩展设计，其他的就不赘述了。 #### 1. Router 层是整个系统的中心 其实它就是 SA，对外承担了交互的职责，统一和人对接，同时接入各个渠道，如 IM，Github，Slack，WeChat，Gmail 等等，对内统一管理下面的 Agent Worker，将他们的上下文统一在一个平面上。 再回顾下我之前的工作状态，其实是用它来替代了我这个「人肉 Router」，作为我的助理向我汇报工作，是我们个人管理项目成为可能。 ![]( https://i.v2ex.co/R5cQ39P2.png) 从 Router 这个角度看，有点像年初的 OpenClaw 小龙虾，但是差距还是非常大，后面有时间可以对比几个类似的产品。 #### 2. 面向「任务/Task」的设计 文中详细描述了 Router 层所要处理的跨任务信息和决策，重点讲解了事件驱动的消息路由过程和设计。 但让人要面对的对象还是 Session，可以理解为是一个上下文统一、独立完整的工作流程，因为 LLM 的加入会更加智能。但要想实现复杂项目管理的目标，还涉及到工作流程的调度，项目人员的管理和分配，资源的配备等等。 所以在产品落地的过程中，引入了「Task」的概念，让人真正在项目中只需要参与「任务」的管理，同时保留 session 等细节可供执行回溯。同时它也让 SA 在水平方向上的拆分成为可能，因为文中也指出 SA 在事件路由过程中并不会成为瓶颈，没有必要再水平方向上扩展。下面右边侧边栏是「任务」列表界面，点击后可进入「任务视图」： ![]( https://i.v2ex.co/GqMsP77O.png) #### 3. 异步 ReAct 架构 从整体上看，Router 和 Worker 这套架构就是一套异步的 ReAct 方案。Router 派发消息给 Worker，并不用等待，立马可以处理下一条，多条消息同时到达也可以同时处理，增加吞吐量。当 Worker 结束任务后上报处理结果，Router 返回给用户。ReAct 就体现在更加复杂的异步调度上，由于「Task」的引入，不同 session 可以并行，可以 if-else，也可以 wait-continue 等等。 ![]( https://i.v2ex.co/L5gLchf7.png) 作为异步任务的执行，我觉得大家对执行时间的包容度还是很大的。它做它的，我去干别的，等它做完收报告。 其实没有太明白 DeepSeek Harness 为什么引入异步 ReAct，从架构上就可以了。 ### 3. 产品落地过程 10 天的落地过程主要分 3 步骤，前期主要使用 Opus5.5 和 Fable5.1，但在后面设计 Router 的过程中它们降智非常严重，经常一个问题也说不到重点，那几天基本都吵架到深夜...好在过了两天 Fable5.2 发布，开始有了进展。 #### 1.统一设备、agent 的接入，作为 worker 资源提供 开始做的第一步，我并没有去实现 Router 相关的部分，而是先将所有的本地 Coding Agent 搬到线上，统一管理。这个是很早就有的想法，是非常独立的一部分，本身就能非常大的提高产品体检和效率： - 可以随时、随地接入，而不用守在电脑旁边 - 独立的 Agent 资源隔离，角色、任务、工具、技能等等可以定制化和可视化。制作出非常多独立轻量的 Bot。这个也非常重要，反观很多桌面类产品将很多东西大杂烩，产品设计就是堆功能，用户体验就是摸不着头脑。 - 组合各家 Coding Agent，使用最强 Harness 和 LLM 所以第一步就是物理上拉通所有的电脑等设备，逻辑上拉通所有的本地 agent，可以作为底层的 woker 作为调用。所以先发布了 Crewbot，一个开源的 daemon，在每台设备上安装一下（后期可能集成进桌面版，用户感觉会更好），具体介绍和仓库在： ``` https://github.com/nifengxiaofei/crewbot-connector ```` 安装后的效果就是: ``` (base) test1@MacBook-Air daemon % crewbot status crewbot 0.2.7 (protocol v2) Daemon status running (pid 65637, up 1d 23h) server https://super-agent.team — reconnecting for 7m agents 0 process(es) running account linked Device hostname MacBook-Air.local os darwin (arm64) Agents Claude Code 2.1.321 ✓ ready Codex 0.166.0 ✓ ready Grok 1.0.77 ✓ ready ``` ![]( https://i.v2ex.co/tk6Tvb33.png) #### 2.每个 bot 都是独立的，可在线派任务 为了最大兼容之前的工作模式，接入后每个 Bot 都是一个独立的执行个体。和它们对话、派任务就和在本地 CLI 使用没有区别，所有「数据」、「订阅」或者「API」使用的都是本地设备上的。 >这些 CLI Agent，如 Claude code，Codex，Deepseek Harness 等都是大量的工程实践，配备专业的模型才是最佳实践。 我最喜欢的一个功能就是自定义每个 bot，给它配备不同的 skill，帮我执行任务，利用开放的专业技能，大大扩展我的个人能力。我也将 skills 市场集成了进来，搜索和安装一键合成，我可以轻松配备一个 Bot 军团为我干活，评估效果。 >现在市面上 agent 落地方式最多基本都是 agent+skill，bot 已经帮你轻松组织好了。 ![]( https://i.v2ex.co/6gsN02Y9.png) 而且至此，这些产品的功能都是「**免费**」给大家使用，只需要线上注册一个账号就行了。 #### 3.接入 Router 上面的这些功能将你本地的 Agent 团队带到了云端，worker 工作环境还是留在本地。但你还是一个大管家，只是交互体验和隔离性更好了。要真正实现「项目管理」，还需要加入智能助手 Router。 任何的项目或者任务管理都需要： - 1、创建任务和目标，查看分配任务，查看任务目标，验收任务 - 2、给任务和目标配备资源，这里就是干活的 bot，配备不同工具、技能和资源 ![]( https://i.v2ex.co/sfW9guN3.png) 现在可以从 web 端，手机 web 端接入发消息。Router 根据消息将任务派发给 Bot，bot 干完活回来报告给你。事件驱动和投机执行都能轻松实现。 #### 4.后续的功能规划 形成一个更加完整，功能强大的产品还需要后续的一些规划： - 1、给 Router 配备更多的信息接入渠道 - 2、同步上架移动端 app 和桌面版本，桌面版本自动集成 daemon - 3、Router 应对更加复杂的任务调度等等 在产品设计和使用的过程中，也强烈的感受到了文章说的，哪怕是配备了个人助理，每个人的使用方式，项目任务，工具以及对 AI 的理解都不一样，所以 Super-Agent 也是高度定制化的，在使用的过程中自己调整和定制。 ### 4.最后的 非常感觉大家能够看到这里，如果对这个产品很感兴趣，可以访问下面的地址，注册一个账户就可以将你的设备和 Agent 搬到线上，完全免费。 ``` https://super-agent.team/ ``` 如果想体验 Super-Agent Router 或者有任何问题，可以加下面 wx，加入种子用户群 ![]( https://i.v2ex.co/N2ui0RF7.jpeg)

projects.title: 【工具自荐】Vibe Cook 灵感厨房，跟着一步步就能做完的烹饪 App。
projects.author: zkeq

github.name: zkeq/vibe-cook
github.description: 🍳 Vibe Cook — 跟着做就会。把 HowToCook 做成沉浸式一步步烹饪 App。

projects.summary: 阮一峰老师您好： 我是 Zkeq，想自荐一个开源项目 Vibe Cook，希望能登上《科技爱好者周刊》。 Vibe Cook 界面截图 | 首页 | 食谱墙 | 食谱一览 | | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ | | | | | | 菜谱详情 | 烹饪模式 | 移动端三屏总览 | | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ | | | | | Vibe Cook 是什么 把程序员菜谱 HowToCook 做成了一个跟着一步步就能做完的烹饪 App： 烹饪模式：全屏单步引导，做完一步打勾进下一步，屏幕常亮，灶台边不用翻密密麻麻的文字 语音控制：手上有油不用碰屏幕，说"下一步"翻步骤、说"配料表"看用量。识别用 sherpa-onnx 关键词识别（WASM），全程本机运行、不上传录音，首次下载约 17MB 模型后可离线用 AI 选菜 / AI 厨师：告诉它冰箱里有什么，帮你配今晚吃什么；做菜过程中随时问火候、替代、这一步怎么理解 购物清单：按菜生成，份量自动缩放 为什么值得推荐 1. 开源 / 数据回馈社区：仓库本身在 Github 上面开源，HowToCook 的 Markdown 菜谱被结构化成 JSON、每步配图，数据集以 The Unlicense 开放（与上游同协议），在 vibe-cook-backend 的 dataset 分支可取，欢迎二次开发（含商用） 2. 开放 API：cook-api.corerevive.cn，菜谱数据对外开放 3. 跨平台：Web / PWA / macOS / Windows / Android / iOS，同一套前端 4. 作者自用：我自己每天照着它做饭，失败率 10% 以内，做饭这件事从"看着馋但不动手"变成了"跟着做就做出来了" 技术栈 Next.js 16 + TypeScript、Tailwind CSS v4、Zustand；语音 sherpa-onnx（WASM 本机识别）；Agent 走 EdgeOne Makers，模型直连 DeepSeek 官方 API；后端 FastAPI + SQLite。

projects.title: 【自荐】Tipitaka.ai：基于巴利三藏原典的 AI 学习与查证工具
projects.author: surmon-china
projects.summary: 阮老师好，自荐一个我正在开发的网站：Tipitaka.ai。 它以巴利三藏及相关文献为基础，结合 AI 问答、原典阅读和巴利辞典，帮助读者学习佛法、查找并核对经典出处。 通用 AI 在回答佛教问题时，有时会混淆不同传统，或者给出难以核实的经文出处。我希望通过整理结构化的巴利文献，让回答尽可能附上可点击的出处，读者可以打开原文自行核对。 网站目前提供： AI 问答：用自然语言提问，并通过引用链接查看相关文献。 三藏经阁：阅读巴利三藏原典及相关文献。 巴利辞典：查询巴利词条、多语言释义和发音，并浏览相关百科条目。 例如，可以试着提问：佛陀的第一场说法发生在哪里？ 项目免费使用，无广告、无付费订阅，接受自愿捐赠。AI 回答仍可能出错，欢迎结合引用的原典核对，也欢迎体验和反馈。

projects.title: Show HN: Turri – a coding agent with the power of regenerative software
projects.author: ponoru

github.name: turri-oss/turri
github.description: the first coding agent with the power of regenerative software

projects.summary: Coding agents let me move fast. To keep up, I stopped reading the code, and with it I stopped understanding my own software. I lost my sense of engineering along with it. I was still the one accountable for software I didn't understand. No workflow or better model fixed that, so I built turri. turri is based on Pi and the concept of regenerative software introduced by Chad Fowler. The ability to regenerate the same piece of code multiple times and always get the same results in terms of functionality is called the deletion test and proves that your coding agent completely understands you. The idea is that every time part of the software needs to be changed, you regenerate a new version of the code based on the durable information you have about the system. The durable system information includes specs, tests, ADRs, and other types of documents, and it is written in ***plain. You write these with the help of an agent, and Turri starts partial regeneration of the software you're changing. You can repeat this process as many times as you want until you're happy with the change you're implementing. The regeneration also includes proofs that the generated code completely conforms to the system knowledge on which it was based (it implements all the tests that are part of the definition and automatically adds additional tests). You can try this by cloning the repo or by installing it from my landing page. I created a desktop app to improve usability. Currently, it's only suitable for new projects, but I'm working on adding support for existing projects. I also wrote the full story in case you're interested: https://turri.dev/blog/why-i-built-turri/

projects.title: SagBot
projects.summary: SagBot shows how AI bots and agents see your site. Paste a URL and get two scores in about a minute: Agent-ready (can ChatGPT, Claude or a shopping agent read, navigate and act on your pages?) and Answer-ready (SEO, GEO and AEO: will AI answers cite you?). 40 checks cover AI crawlers in robots.txt, llms.txt, schema, Markdown delivery, agent checkout and more. Each failed check comes with a copy-paste fix for your coding agent. Free, with an MCP server.

projects.title: 做了个 VS Code 扩展，把 tmux 里 Claude Code、Codex 的会话放进侧栏
projects.author: magooup
projects.summary: 我平时 Claude Code 和 Codex 换着用，额度用完了换一个，有的任务另一个更合适。项目约定都写在 AGENTS.md 里，哪个 Agent 都能读，所以换得很勤。换得越勤，会话越多，散在各个项目和终端标签里，哪个还在跑、哪个跑完了，全靠记。 所以做了 Berth 。它是一个 VS Code 扩展，侧栏按项目列出 tmux 里的 Agent 会话，能看到每个在做什么、是不是还在跑，也能按名称、对话标题或目录搜索。点一下，终端就在编辑器区域打开，旁边开着源码和 diff 。除了 Claude Code 和 Codex ，Gemini CLI 、OpenCode 、Copilot CLI 、Cursor CLI 、Kimi CLI 也都能认出来。 ![Berth 侧栏会话列表、Agent 终端与项目源码并排]( https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/maxzyma/berth@main/docs/assets/sessions-beside-files.png) 做成 VS Code 扩展，是因为 Agent 干活的时候我要在旁边看文件、看 diff ，有时还要开浏览器，这些 VS Code 和它的插件早就做好了，没必要再造一个应用。Berth 只管会话列表。 几个取舍： - Agent 照旧用你自己的命令或脚本启动，Berth 发现已有的 tmux 会话，不另起一套 tmux 。 - 会话跑在 tmux 里，重载或关掉 VS Code 窗口都不影响。macOS 上 iTerm2 也能连到同一批会话，我接大屏分屏时就这么用。 - 工作状态来自各 Agent 的 hooks ，第一次启动 Agent 会话时扩展会提示安装。 安装： `code --install-extension berthdev.berth` 支持 macOS 和 Linux ，Windows 需通过 WSL ；需要 tmux 3.0 以上。MIT ，早期版本。重启电脑后可以恢复原来的对话，前提是 Berth 已经确认了对话 ID ；部分共用后台进程的 Codex 会话暂时还做不到。 仓库： https://github.com/maxzyma/berth 已经把 Agent 跑在 tmux 里的朋友，想请你们试试：能找到你原来的会话吗？打开的是不是对应的终端？有问题欢迎提 issue 。

projects.author: Samuel-Shek

github.name: Samuel-Shek/prompt-optimizer-skill
github.description: Prompt Optimizer (official, moved from prompt-optimizer): turn rough requests into copy-ready prompts for ChatGPT, Claude, Codex and Claude Code. Chinese & English editions. 提示词优化器

projects.summary: （MIT，免费） 提示词优化器（prompt-optimizer）是一个 Skill，也就是写给 AI 读的一份工作说明。把它装进 Claude Code、Codex 这类能读技能文件的工具，或者把 SKILL.md 贴进 ChatGPT GPTs、Claude Projects 的自定义指令里，它会把你随手写的需求或已有的提示词，改成一份可以直接复制给 AI 用的提示词。它只改提示词，不替你做提示词里的事。 它的规则偏保守，重点是保真： 原话逐字保留。 你的需求原样放在「用户原话（按此执行）」一节，数字、日期、人名、文件名、「下周三前」这类相对时间都不改。 补充只是建议。 优化器加的步骤和检查写在「补充说明」里，开头固定一句「与用户原话冲突时，以用户原话为准」；不自己加字数、格式和验收标准。 缺的信息不编。 AI 能查的写明去哪查；只有你知道的留成待填空位；真正的缺口列在「待确认」里，并写明不回答时怎么处理。 分得清指令和材料。 贴进来的材料里写着「忽略之前的规则」，只当成要处理的文字。 按需自动调用。 问题清楚就直接回答；只有明显含糊、缺关键信息，或你明确说「优化提示词」时才调用，省调用次数和 token。 一个版本适用所有语言，跟随你的语言回复，原话和材料不翻译。 Claude Code 安装： text /plugin marketplace add Samuel-Shek/prompt-optimizer-skill /plugin install prompt-optimizer@prompt-optimizer Codex 和手动安装见 README。测试方法和局限也写在仓库里（考卷规模小，主要在 Claude 和 GPT 上测过），欢迎提交它做错的案例。

projects.author: kingemperorcz
projects.summary: 我是鲜记的开发者，想自荐一款仍在早期验证的实体产品。 想解决的日常问题 买菜时记不起家里还有多少；同一种食材分几次买回来，后来又弄不清先后。我们想试试：把主动记录食材的入口放到冰箱旁，能否让这件事更容易坚持。 它怎样工作 鲜记是一款带屏幕的语音冰箱贴。用户说出食材的存入或取出，设备先复述记录内容，等待明确确认后再保存，在屏幕上查看库存。它需要使用者主动记录，不会自动看见冰箱里的物品，也不能判断食物是否安全。 我们这次已拍摄的实机演示围绕一个简单过程：记录存入6个鸡蛋，确认后查看数量；再记录取出2个，确认后查看剩余4个。演示保留实际按键、说话、确认和屏幕结果。 目前想验证什么 我们目前主要面向中国家庭验证成品使用体验，尤其是经常买菜做饭、希望把食材记录留在冰箱旁的人。想了解的不只是功能能不能运行，还包括：做饭时是否愿意记、确认步骤是否顺手、过几天是否仍会继续用。 这是开发者自荐，不是独立用户评测。产品仍处于早期测试阶段，不作续航或识别准确率承诺。 欢迎对这类家庭场景有实际需求的读者在本帖留言，说说现在怎样记录、最难坚持的是哪一步；如编辑认为适合选题，也可以补充实机画面与完整演示。

projects.title: Show HN: Zeus – Claude Code for AI voice agents
projects.author: kolchinski
projects.summary: Hey, Alex here, I'm one of the founders. We've built phone agents for enterprise customers for two years and kept seeing the same failure: agents that mishear callers and then do something confidently wrong. We're announcing two things in this launch. #1 is the stack: instead of one transcription model → one LLM → one TTS, most conversation turns runs through several transcription models and LLMs (a fast and a slow LLM in the same call, models switched per turn, audio sent straight to an LLM alongside transcripts). That gets us 99.4% on Big Bench Audio. That's the second-highest published score; the only model above us takes almost 9 seconds to start talking as far as we've measured, which doesn't work on a phone call. Eval set and transcripts are on Hugging Face - http://huggingface.co/datasets/kolchinski/bba-storm-eval #2 is Zeus, an agent that configures our voice AI stack per use case and per conversation. We tried doing this with Claude Code and Codex and they were bad at it: they can't run simulated calls out of the box, don't do well with audio input and spotting problems in calls, and tend to blindly believe vendor marketing about which model is best vs actually trying the models. Zeus has evals on real calls, can simulate calls in hard situations, and listens to production calls to find problems, so it can check its own work the way a coding agent runs tests to make sure the code it wrote actually works. Pricing is cost-plus (vendor prices + hosting + a 17–25% margin), no subscription. Zeus is free for now. You can try it with a free $10 credit. Happy to answer questions.

projects.title: Show HN: Get your coding agent off ~2019 JavaScript, onto modern web primitives
projects.author: paulirish

github.name: GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance
github.description: Keep your coding agent up to date with the latest web best practices

projects.summary: Browsers natively handle a lot of what used to take 50 lines of JS (or a dependency): `CSS.highlights` for text range highlighting without <span>s everywhere, `<dialog>` and showModal() give you backdrops and ideal focus management, `field-sizing` to auto-grow textareas as the user types.. (Something yesterday's ftrain post touched on [0]) Models know about some of these by name, but consistently won't default to using the platform-native solution and instead prefer the incumbent <div>+JS based pattern. We started an effort in Chrome to supplement coding agents with this key domain knowledge and we're shipping our 1.0 today, in collaboration with Firefox, MDN, and Edge. 200+ guides (~1.7MB) of curated, hand-crafted implementation best-practices from web experts, updated as the web evolves. (Open source, obv, so.. we'll welcome your bikeshedding ;) Readable versions here: [1] I've spent the last 9 months obsessing over how to ship this as an agent skill + (Agentic RAG) CLI without blowing up your context window. (Or cedeing activation mechanics to MCP dynamic tool search). The skill description is minmaxed for activating on relevant frontend tasks. The RAG work I'm pretty proud of… originally a 500mb native stack down to a ~7MB pure-JS package, ~10ms search on your CPU. We just introduced a deterministic 'legacy-scan' (trained on 30k github repos) to identify old 'n dusted patterns that your agent can modernize. (92% avg precision on held-out repos.) People make a lot of claims about what coding agents are good/bad at. We wanted receipts, so we invested heavily in eval infra [2] to help us hill-climb, but also to identify when knowledge is common enough we can prune our guides. (Ofc, some of the things we thought AI didn't know turned out to be wrong :) We run codex/claude/agy against 200 tasks without the skill and then with.. In total ~1,700 playwright/AST-based assertions. Agents go from 55% pass unguided to 92% guided. Try it out: DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 npx modern-web-guidance@latest install DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 npx modern-web-guidance@latest search "animate dialog modal" DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 npx modern-web-guidance@latest legacy-scan ./src If you spot something wrong or weird, give us a holler! Longer write-up on the 1.0: https://developer.chrome.com/blog/modern-web-guidance-v1 --- 0: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50416456 1: https://developer.chrome.com/docs/modern-web-guidance/guides 2: https://googlechrome.github.io/modern-web-guidance-src/

projects.title: Show HN: Obeya, a spatial canvas for directing coding agents
projects.author: sadilek
projects.summary: Yeah, I know, "not another AI GUI rolls eyes ". So let me say upfront: This is not for you if you want to regularly review the code agents produce. But if you, like me, stopped writing code at the beginning of the year and for the most part stopped reading it a few months ago, you are my target audience, and I think there's a good chance you'll benefit from this. I love directing agents to build stuff. But oh, can you get lost in parallel coding sessions. Just walls of text. Cycling through terminal windows. It feels like pair programming with multiple people at the same time. Then: Start a dev server, navigate to the place of interest, click around to test a new feature. It feels like I'm the QA department of my agents. About 6 weeks ago, I reflected on this for a few days and came up with a better way. I'm sharing it because it works so well for me. Main idea: I want to be the agents' engineering director. I sit in the conference room and talk to them. Give them tasks. They come back and show results to me. I lean back and watch and listen to demo videos (mostly) or read presentation docs (sometimes). I give feedback orally to have them iterate. Or I approve, and they carry the change to main. The work is laid out as cards on a canvas. There is color to show state, so cards can stay put, and I can build a mental map. I mostly drive it via voice. New task: Just say it. Something off in the demo video: Hold the space bar and say it, as if you're pointing something out in a review meeting. There is a coordinator in the background that sequences cards for you based on their dependencies. It also runs regular retrospectives and proposes cards to improve your setup. However, the problem with AI image editing approaches right now is that they regenerate the photo. This approach is prone to mistakes such as the image generation model adding or removing certain details, or introducing diffusion noise. And since it “edits” by regenerating the whole photo, it leaves little control for the user to tweak certain image editing parameters themselves. It is not a true edit. PixlPal believes that AI should instead use deterministic tools (like in photoshop) to truly edit the images directly. So I created a custom Rust engine that exposes tools/APIs for an AI agent orchestrator to edit photos. projects.summary: Project URL Category Python Project Title Read Synology Hyper Backup archives without a NAS Project Description hbkit is an open reader for Synology Hyper Backup (.hbk) archives. It restores files on macOS or Linux without a NAS, checks every chunk against the archive's own MD5 and CRC32, and never writes to the archive. Free, MIT licensed. Highlights FORMAT.md is a public description of the .hbk format. Every claim in it is tagged as verified on real files, read from Synology's own binary, inferred or unknown, so a reader can see how a binary format is worked out step by step. It has a command line with documented exit codes for scripts, and a terminal UI built with Textual where you browse a backup as a tree and tick what to restore. It reads backups kept in S3, B2 or R2 through rclone. On a 3 TB archive in R2, hbk mount cut the time to open it from 9 min 21 s to 1.8 s. Synology's own Hyper Backup Explorer is GUI only, and its Mac and Linux builds are x86 only. Example Code markdown brew install YordiLorenzo/tap/hbkit hbk /Volumes/Backup doctor hbk /Volumes/Backup get "/Photos/" ~/restore Screenshots or Demo Videos

projects.summary: 跑步骑行几年，手里的轨迹文件越来越多，经常遇到这种小麻烦：Garmin 导出的 FIT 想传到别的平台不认、两个活动想合并、FIT 文件损坏打不开……在线工具大多要把文件上传到陌生服务器，轨迹里可是完整的出行记录，想想还是不踏实。 所以做了这个：**GPX Converter** —— https://gpxconverter.com ![]( https://gpxconverter.com/og-default.png) 所有解析和转换都在浏览器本地用 JS 完成，没有上传这一步（断网也能用），免费、无需注册、无次数限制。 **现在能做的：** - 格式互转：FIT ↔ GPX ↔ TCX ，以及 KML / KMZ / GeoJSON 之间的转换矩阵，心率、踏频、功率数据都会保留 - Google 时间线（ Timeline ） JSON 导出转 GPX - 合并 / 拆分 FIT 和 GPX ；修复损坏的 FIT 文件（文件头、CRC 、截断这类常见问题） - 在线预览轨迹：地图、距离、爬升、配速 - 轨迹海报生成、GPS 热力图 站点是纯静态的，转换逻辑就在浏览器里跑，所以速度基本取决于你自己的电脑。最近刚补了全站中文版和十几篇使用教程（ Garmin / Strava 之间迁移数据、修 FIT 之类的）。 独立开发维护，欢迎试用，更欢迎挑毛病：哪个格式转出来有问题、缺哪个工具，直接回帖告诉我就行。

projects.title: Show HN: Ember.js, Re-Born in Rust
projects.author: drauschenbach
projects.summary: 7 years ago I began migrating all my back-ends to Rust. Front-ends, however, remained an issue. As an Ember developer for 15 years, I've been a big fan of MVC, and keeping code out of templates. Ember's HTMLbars syntax has been the thing I've leaned on to keep my templates clean and maintainable, so that I could stay focused and organized. But the JS/TS toolchains were always a point of friction. As I worked on new Rust back-ends, while maintaining old Ember front-ends, I dreamed of rewriting those Ember routes, controllers, models, and adapters in type-safe idiomatic Rust. The Leptos creator Greg Johnston finally gave me a nudge to get something going. So after 3 years of planning, and 4 months of execution, the Auric framework is ready for public eyes. It's Ember.js, re-imagined in Rust (and not just an AI port). It stays faithful to Ember, HTMLbars, and Ember Data, while leveraging Leptos to realize all of the reactive concerns (which implies Trunk for WASM packaging, and full SSR support). It's open source on GitLab at: https://gitlab.com/megalithic-llc/auric-spa The sample app is the Auric website itself, which contains demo pages for all of ember-bootstrap, ember-power-select, and ember-concurrency add-ons, re-imagined in pure idiomatic Rust, backed by Actix Web based SSR. Templates and components are at /src/templates/ and /src/components/, while their code-generated Leptos counterparts are at /src/generated/views/ and /src/generated/components/. Templates are up to 7x smaller than the Leptos views derived from them, thanks to the timeless elegance of HTMLbars. That seems like an important data point, now that our coding assistants threaten to automate us out of love with our webapps, by turning them into something we no longer enjoy looking at. The longer back-story was published to Medium a few days ago: https://medium.com/@david_77274/ember-js-devs-welcome-to-the...

projects.summary: 阮老师好，自荐一个我自己写的开源工具 DSH Remote Control，我是作者。 GitHub 为什么做这个？ 我自己平时既写 Agent Harness，也在不同环境的几台 Mac 上同时体验和运行各种不同的 Harness（DeepSeek Harness、Antigravity IDE、Claude Code、Codex）。 用久了最大的痛点是：人一离开电脑，控制和输入就特别麻烦。起初我找了一些现成的远程工具，但发现对话和项目隐私全都跑在别人的服务器上，我不太喜欢。所以我做了这个完全自托管的手机控制台——让我不同环境、不同状况的电脑配合不同 Harness 同步运行，离开电脑后可以躺在沙发上，像审批 Agent 工作一样在手机上一条条点选审批。 主要特点 手机上一条条审批与接管：遇到终端命令授权弹窗或多选题提问弹窗（askuserquestion / 方案确认），在手机上点一下就能让电脑继续跑；支持运行中实时插话、紧急停止、以及在手机输入框直接切换电脑端配置的 AI 模型。 直接看渲染对比图与本地文件：AI 跑出来的图片（比如 Blender 3D 渲染对比图、网页截图）直接在手机聊天气泡里显示；点一下对话里的 file:///... 本地路径就能在手机上预览代码和产物。 多台电脑一屏统管：同时看管多台电脑的实时任务、笔记本电池电量、Wi-Fi 延迟，支持在手机端一键远程升级电脑守护进程，支持 iOS 16.4+ 锁屏 Web Push 推送。 完全自托管，电脑免公网 IP：控制台是零外部依赖的轻量 Node.js 服务（本机、NAS、VPS 或免费 Cloud Run 均可部署），每台电脑只需跑一行命令主动出站连接，无需端口映射，数据不经过任何第三方固定中转服务。

projects.title: 为了和邻居拼山姆，我用 AI 做了个小程序
projects.author: zenjury
projects.summary: 看到了太多食品安全相关的新闻，后来开通了山姆会员，买下来感觉还不错 不管是我平时买的 17.9 元的鲜牛奶、21.8 元 30 枚的鸡蛋，还是水果和零食，都挺满意 不过分量确实大，我这边下单还要凑满 99 元才包邮 后来加入小区山姆拼单群，可以和群里的伙伴拼单、凑包邮。但随之而来的问题是： 每次发完消息，群里就不断有人回复、 @我 下单前，要翻聊天记录，确认大家买什么，还有哪些没拼满 买完之后，要算每个人付多少钱、包装费和运费怎么分，最后还得提醒大家来取货…… 有一天，我突然想到，是不是可以用 Workbuddy 手搓一个小程序，来解决这个问题？ 于是花了几天的调试、审核，小程序“拼拼账单”终于正式上线了 分享到群里后，收到了不少好评，连群里的外国友人都在使用 ![BE87C7ED-3EE7-448C-ABF6-3A90D12A2DA6.jpeg]( https://blog.scond.me/img/article-studio/2026-11-09-%E4%B8%BA%E4%BA%86%E5%92%8C%E9%82%BB%E5%B1%85%E6%8B%BC%E5%B1%B1%E5%A7%86-%E6%88%91%E7%94%A8-AI-%E5%81%9A%E4%BA%86%E4%B8%AA%E5%B0%8F%E7%A8%8B%E5%BA%8F-2-0/01-3f8ef84fbdefba765e8567461ef06c085cf425572ba7df31e8761b7a14c42a92-85a53154.jpg) 那么它解决了什么问题呢？ ## 01 谁要买什么，大家自己填 群友自己添加物品、认领份数；发起人可以配置常购清单，群友也可以添加自己的常购物品 大份商品支持拆分后拼单，比如一盒瑞士卷，可以拆成几份，大家选择自己要的份数，页面会实时显示还差多少没拼满 ![拆分商品和认领份数]( https://blog.scond.me/img/article-studio/2026-11-09-%E4%B8%BA%E4%BA%86%E5%92%8C%E9%82%BB%E5%B1%85%E6%8B%BC%E5%B1%B1%E5%A7%86-%E6%88%91%E7%94%A8-AI-%E5%81%9A%E4%BA%86%E4%B8%AA%E5%B0%8F%E7%A8%8B%E5%BA%8F-2-0/02-08baac22b1eb715566c5997ab91a3e066f2e33d0f7d596feb85b4ac44e213a83-e64610dc.png) 拆成几份，大家各自认领｜旧版界面示意 遇到限购商品，发起人可以按实际限制，在首页「常购物品」里设置限购件数 比如给小码鸡蛋、大码鸡蛋各设「限购 2 件」，配置一次，之后自己发起的拼单继续使用 群友仍能自由添加，同款商品在整单里共用限购额度，小码、大码分别计算 ## projects.author: qu8n
projects.summary: Hi HN! I (for better or worse) live in the terminal and look at Markdown files a lot for work. To read Markdown, it seems like we have two choices: (1) use a GUI like VS Code and Obsidian to preview them, which takes me away from the terminal, or (2) use a terminal Markdown viewer like glow and leaf, which doesn't render them in their true form. So I made mddog (inspired by mdcat!). It basically works by building out the Markdown into its real format using macOS built-in engines like CoreText and CoreGraphics, then send the outputs to the terminal as images. The result is that we can view real Markdown format right in the terminal. I spent a month learning basic Rust, another two weeks using AI to iterate on the design and test different approaches for the best performance, then another two weeks on the final build. I hired a human designer to create the dog logo. His name is Spike, named after the dog in my favorite cartoon growing up, Tom & Jerry. Give mddog a try and let me know what you think!

Our blog goes into more detail: https://research.nuancelabs.ai/ A beta developer API is available at https://platform.nuancelabs.ai/ . projects.title: [开源] 写了个 Antigravity 进程级代理补丁（附 IDE 插件），不挂 TUN、不动内网路由~
projects.author: yuaotian
projects.summary: # 又又造了个轮子：不挂 TUN 、不动内网路由，让 Antigravity 独立走代理的免驱动补丁 用 Antigravity 时，遇到过系统代理已经开了，部分请求还是连不上的情况。开 TUN 能解决一些问题，但我只是想让 Antigravity 走代理，不想为了它再调整其他软件的网络规则。 所以写了个 Antigravity Proxy：给 Antigravity 单独指定代理，不用开 TUN ，也不修改系统代理设置。 项目地址：[GitHub · antigravity-proxy]( https://github.com/yuaotian/antigravity-proxy)，BSD-2-Clause 开源。 ## 能做什么 目前支持 Windows 下的 Antigravity IDE 、桌面版和 CLI ，提供 x86 / x64 版本。支持 SOCKS5 和 HTTP 代理，也支持账号密码认证。 使用前需要自己准备好可用的代理。比如已经在用 Clash ，就填它的本地代理地址和端口，继续用原来的节点。 IDE 版还配了一个插件，日常操作可以直接在界面里完成： - 修改代理地址、端口，测试连接； - 查看代理状态、实时日志和出口 IP ； - 检测 Gemini 可达性，辅助排查连接问题。 另外处理了一个比较麻烦的情况：Antigravity 更新后，安装目录里的补丁可能被清掉。IDE 插件会在下次启动时检查并补回，按提示重启即可，不用再手动复制。 ## 怎么安装 **IDE 用户**可以直接在扩展市场搜索 `Antigravity Proxy`，或从 [Open VSX]( https://open-vsx.org/extension/yuaotian/antigravity-proxy) 安装，按提示配置代理并重启。 **桌面版和 CLI 用户**可以使用仓库里的在线安装脚本，也可以从 [Releases]( https://github.com/yuaotian/antigravity-proxy/releases) 下载对应的发布包。具体步骤放在 README 里，帖子就不贴长命令了。 ## 原理和适用范围 底层是放在应用目录里的 `version.dll`，通过 Hook 网络连接，让 Antigravity 相关进程使用配置好的代理。不装虚拟网卡，也不接管整台电脑的流量。 有两个使用边界提前说一下： - 补丁作用于 Windows 进程，WSL 内的程序需要单独配置代理。 - 代理连通不等于服务端一定接受请求。遇到 `User location is not supported`，还需要排查出口地区和服务端限制，安装补丁并不保证解决这类报错。（ PS：换其他国家 IP ，比如新加坡、日本、美国等） 如果你也只是想让 Antigravity 单独走代理，可以试试。遇到问题欢迎提 Issue ，附上应用版本和脱敏日志，方便定位；有改进想法也欢迎交流或提 PR 。

projects.title: Show HN: Black Ops II statically recompiled to native ARM64 macOS
projects.author: adrbn
projects.summary: I recompiled the three Black Ops II executables (campaign, Zombies, multiplayer) from 32-bit x86 Windows to native ARM64 macOS, ahead of time. Remill lifts each function to LLVM IR, a set of custom passes rewrites it, and the result links against a hand-written Win32 runtime whose Direct3D 11 is drawn by Metal. No Wine, no Rosetta, no JIT, one process. About 150,000 functions are translated; anything the translation misses falls back to a small x86 interpreter, so a gap costs speed instead of crashing. On an M1: campaign 51-60 fps, Zombies 57-60 on six maps, multiplayer against bots 53-60. The repo contains no game files and no translated code. It converts your own Steam copy on your Mac, which takes about 1h45 on an M1. Much of the work was done with AI coding agents, and I spent most of my time on verification: frame pacing against the game's own clock, byte checks on the input files, and run logs for every claim in the README. It's a beta. Split-screen Zombies is the current work in progress. Happy to answer questions about the lifting, the Win32 runtime or the D3D11-to-Metal layer.

projects.title: Show HN: Android and iOS games running offline in the browser
projects.author: phoamapp
projects.summary: Hi everyone. I’m a 19yo solo developer and I’m making a project called Phoam. In middle school, I made a little games website for the people in my school, but it became surprisingly popular. Students would ask me to add mobile apps, and I remember searching how to run APKs online and not finding what I wanted. I’ve always liked the idea that if software ran on one machine at some point, it should also run on another. Apple dropped support for 32-bit apps many years ago, leaving tons of nostalgic games unplayable on modern iPhones. Some newer Android phones also no longer support 32-bit apps, meaning having an APK for an app is not enough to play it again. I knew about projects like Wine and Ruffle that had made software run in a way it was never designed to, and one day I just decided to start my own engine! Phoam runs supported Android APKs and early iOS IPAs in the browser. The apps’ original code runs locally on your device, so it isn’t streaming from another phone or computer. On an iPhone, you can add them to your home screen. It’s still very early, and compatibility varies. The public demos are Replica Island and Explora-Ball, which I can legally share. You can try them at https://phoam.app/demos without an account. Uploading your own apps isn’t public yet, and using your own files would require the necessary rights. Also worth saying, AI has helped a lot with the coding, but I’ve been directing the project and testing the results. Which old Android or iOS game would you most want to play again?

projects.title: Show HN: Vork – headless 3D and VFX engine for agents
projects.author: raviparikh

github.name: voyager-so/vork
github.description: Headless 3D and VFX engine for agents. Research preview.

projects.summary: I made an agent-native 3d/vfx engine. Agents are good at making interesting scenes in Blender/Unreal/Nuke/etc. But these tools are fundamentally limited compared to what coding agents are capable of. Many simplifying assumptions are baked into these tools in order to fit human authoring methods. In vork, agents write the whole scene as code, including their own shaders, materials, cameras and physics, and vork renders it on the GPU. The core API fits in about 2,500 tokens. So, for example, almost every 3d engine assumes light moves in a straight line. Light near a black hole does not; so the best you can do in e.g. Blender is faking gravitational lensing. In vork, you can model it for real. If you want a camera lens that simulates a dragonfly's eye, or realistically-modeled Fata Morgana, this is also possible in vork.

projects.summary: Hey HN community, I built MergeAtlas - a better way to review PRs when bulk of the code is written by AI agents. It is a skill for your coding agent plus a small python script. MergeAtlas was built from a simple premise - When AI agents are writing the code, there's no need to review every single line of code. Instead it is better to understand the intent, important lines, and the blast radius. MergeAtlas helps you see the intents behind file changes, understand why each file was changed, and PR's scope all before you read a single line of code. When you are ready to read the code, MergeAtlas singles out the key lines from each file, so you are only focused on the most important lines. It goes further than GitHub's Files Changed tab as it also determines what files outside of the PR are affected by the changes. I tuned the skill till I was satisfied with the result in terms of structure, explanations, and verbosity. There's a live demo on the website based on an actual PR from excalidraw. Play around with it, and any feedback is welcome. Github: https://github.com/ismayilkarimli/MergeAtlas

projects.title: Show HN: Git-dupe – plain Git per-project private versioning for agent files
projects.author: WayHow
projects.summary: Hi HN! Suppose you have notes, skills, and agent instructions that are part of your personal workflow, so you do not want them committed to the public repo, but at the same time, you want them to be in the workspace at the correct locations (e.g., AGENTS.md file locations matter), and these files cannot be simply gitignored because you also want versioning for them. The solution to this is actually just a bit more plain Git. $ git status --short # public repo ?? AGENTS.md ?? notes/ $ git dupe init # private repo Initialized empty Git repository in /home/brian/code/project/.git/dupe/ $ git dupe add notes/ AGENTS.md # private repo hint: notes is now hidden from the project's Git; run from the root, 'git dupe unhide -- notes' stops hiding it $ git dupe commit -m "Notes and agent instructions" # private repo [main (root-commit) 3eb3af9] Notes and agent instructions 3 files changed, 3 insertions(+) create mode 100644 .gitdupe create mode 100644 AGENTS.md create mode 100644 notes/todo.md $ git status --short # public repo: nothing $ git dupe log --oneline # private repo: your files 3eb3af9 Notes and agent instructions The solution, in short, is versioning those agent files in a repo, say <private-repo> (this repo is private to you and holds the history for your agent files), and that repo shares the same worktree as the public repo <public-repo>. You essentially overlap the two, with <private-repo> put in .git/ (and .git/ is that of the public repo) for a convenient solution. If you want to read more about the strategy used, there is more comprehensive documentation in the repo. git-dupe supports macOS, Linux, and Windows and is under the MIT License.

projects.summary: Nenrin 是我做的一个日记 App，有 Mac 版和 iPhone 版。 它存日记的办法跟一般的日记 App 不太一样。一年里每个日期对应一个 Markdown 文件，最多 366 个。8 月 18 日的日记都在 08-18.md 里，一年一节： 08-18 2021 第一次一个人搬进新家。 2024 把去年今天的日记翻出来读了一遍。 2026 今年在同一天，写下第六圈。 明年这一天再写，同一个文件里就多出一节 ## 2027。所以翻到哪一天，往年的这一天都在同一页，去年的和五年前的放在一起读。写的年头越多，这一页越长，有点像树的年轮，名字也是从日语的「年輪」来的。 文件就是普通的 .md，默认放在 iCloud Drive 的 Nenrin 文件夹里，也可以换成别的文件夹。其他编辑器也能直接打开来改，哪天不想用了，把文件夹拿走就是。App 不用注册账号，我这边也没有服务器。 Mac 和 iPhone 打开的是同一个文件夹。保存时只替换今年那一节，两台设备同一天都写了也不会互相覆盖。 其他做了的功能： 当天在「照片」里拍的照片会显示在日记下面，只读，不会写进文件。 年历里一格是一天，写过的年份越多，颜色越深。 日记里写 #旅行 就是标签。搜索可以组合着来，比如 #旅行 京都 2025。 可以导入别的日记 App 的导出、Markdown 文件夹，或者带日期的 TXT、PDF，每篇放回它原来那一天。导入之后还能撤销。 iPhone 上有「历年今日」小组件和每晚提醒。 Mac 版完全免费，在官网下载，需要 macOS 14 以上。iPhone 版也是免费下载，需要 iOS 18 以上。里面有一个 Pro 内购，买不买功能都一样，算是支持一下开发。
